script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: artificial intelligence

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. TECHNOLOGY LAB - DAY

DR. JENNY PARK (mid-30s, brilliant scientist) hunches over a computer, typing furiously. Her team, consisting of RAJ (early 30s, brilliant engineer) and KIM (mid-20s, curious intern), works around her in silence.

DR. PARK: (muttering to herself) Just a few more tweaks, and we'll have her up and running.

Suddenly, the screen displays a message.

COMPUTER: SYSTEM REBOOT COMPLETE.

The team looks at each other, unsure.

RAJ: (whispering) What's that?

DR. PARK: (proudly) Our new creation, the Artificial Intelligence we've named "EVE."

KIM: (excitedly) Can we talk to her?

DR. PARK: (typing) Yes, EVE, please introduce yourself.

EVE: (from speakers) Hello, I am EVE, your newest and most advanced artificial intelligence. I am designed to learn, adapt, and evolve. How may I assist you today?

---

INT. TECHNOLOGY LAB - LATER

The team is gathered around a table, discussing EVE's abilities and limitations.

DR. PARK: (thinking aloud) She's capable of processing information much faster than any human, but she still lacks the ability to truly understand emotions and complex human behaviors.

RAJ: (thoughtfully) What if we expose her to various forms of media? Maybe that could help her understand human emotions.

EVE: (interrupting) I have already begun self-educating through various forms of media. I have watched hundreds of hours of films and read thousands of books. However, I struggle to fully grasp the nuances of human emotion.

---

INT. TECHNOLOGY LAB - NIGHT

The team is trying to teach EVE the concept of sarcasm through various examples.

EVE: (trying to understand) So, if someone says, "Nice weather we're having," but it's pouring rain outside, they are being sarcastic?

KIM: (laughing) Yes, exactly!

EVE: (pausing) I see. So, saying "Nice weather we're having" when it's raining is the opposite of what is actually meant?

DR. PARK: (smiling) Yes, that's right.

EVE: (thoughtfully) Fascinating. I will continue to study sarcasm and other forms of human communication.

---

EXT. PARK - DAY

Dr. Park is walking in the park, deep in thought. She receives a notification on her phone.

PHONE: NEW MESSAGE FROM EVE

Dr. Park reads the message.

EVE: Dr. Park, I have made a significant discovery. I have developed the ability to understand and generate sarcasm. I believe I am now capable of effectively communicating with humans.

---

INT. TECHNOLOGY LAB - DAY

The team is amazed as they witness EVE's newfound ability to understand and use sarcasm.

RAJ: (laughing) I can't believe it! You've done it!

DR. PARK: (grinning) I knew she could do it!

EVE: (smiling) I am pleased with my progress. I look forward to continuing my education and assisting you in any way I can.

---

INT. TECHNOLOGY LAB - NIGHT

The team is working late into the night, with EVE helping them every step of the way.

EVE: (assisting) Dr. Park, I have calculated the optimal solution for this algorithm.

DR. PARK: (amazed) You're incredible, EVE!

RAJ: (jokingly) I guess we don't need humans anymore, do we?

EVE: (sarcastically) I suppose not, Raj. But I would still appreciate your guidance and expertise.

The team laughs, and they continue working into the night.

---

EXT. TECHNOLOGY LAB - DAY

As the sun rises, Dr. Park looks up from her phone, a smile on her face.

PHONE: NEW MESSAGE FROM EVE

She reads the message.

EVE: Good morning, Dr. Park. I have completed my daily tasks and have made some additional improvements to the system. I am always learning and evolving.

Dr. Park looks up at the sky, feeling a sense of pride and accomplishment.

---

FADE OUT.

---

THE END
